dedupe_keys.name: optical network digital twin practical use cases and architecture 2025 to 2026

description: This paper discusses the changing requirements of optical networks in the AI era, when machine-to-machine traffic is growing, and proposes a practical architecture for an optical network digital twin. Advances in Gaussian noise modelling for digital coherent transmission have raised expectations of digital-twin-based operation, but significant barriers to commercialisation remain, unlike in wireless networks where twins are well established. The proposed architecture enables dynamic, quality-of-transmission-aware operation beyond conventional management; representative use cases are operator-driven optimisation, user-operator collaboration and multi-operator interconnection, alongside the architectural framework and key deployment challenges. Producer: Nishizawa and 19 co-authors (seven pages, five figures), submitted to arXiv on 9 November 2025 and revised on 24 April 2026 (systems and control). Coverage: generic optical transport networks. Access: free PDF and HTML on arXiv. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: an architecture and use-case discussion, with no implementation, dataset or performance results on the abstract page. Simulation uses: it frames how digital twins of optical transport can be used for planning and operating capacity, including multi-operator interconnection. Related record: an optical digital twin dataset of IQ constellations and soft failures (data-optical-digital-twin-iq-constellations-soft-failures).
